rule_context:
Export Control Compliance Note - Denied Party Screening

Scope: All outbound shipments and deemed exports.

Screening requirement: Every consignee, end-user, and intermediate party on a sales order must be screened against the current Consolidated Screening List (CSL) before any booking, BOL issuance, or carrier tender.

Match logic: The screening tool returns exact and fuzzy matches. A fuzzy match includes any variation in legal suffixes (Co., Co, Ltd, Ltd., Inc, Corp), punctuation, spacing, or transliteration that leaves the core commercial name identical. Any fuzzy match against a denied, debarred, or otherwise restricted party entry is treated as a positive hit.

Action on hit: The sales order is placed on compliance hold automatically. No shipment documents may be generated, no PRO number assigned, and no carrier pickup scheduled until Trade Compliance clears the hold in writing.

Clearance process: The assigned rep opens a compliance case in the Trade Compliance queue with the SO number, the screened name, the list entry matched, and the match score. Trade Compliance reviews and either (a) confirms a true party match and maintains the denial, or (b) documents a false positive with supporting evidence and releases the hold. Only case closure with a release disposition lifts the hold.

No exceptions: Urgency, customer pressure, historical shipping history, or "probability" assessments do not override the hold. The rule is binary: hit equals hold until Trade Compliance clears.
